structured_data.title: Brave
structured_data.description: Set in Scotland in a rugged and mythical time, this movie features Princess Merida (Kelly Macdonald), an aspiring archer and impetuous daughter of Queen Elinor (Dame Emma Thompson). Merida makes a reckless choice that unleashes unintended peril and forces her to spring into action to set things right.

community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Brave"] 3/10Не люблю прог-рок, поэтому никогда не слушал Marillion внимательно, но зато очень люблю режиссера Ричарда Стэнли, который снял по альбому этой английской группы концептуальный музыкальный фильм. До этого он снял замечательное кино Hardware и неплохой Dust Devi, но тут повернул куда-то совсем не туда. Мало того, что альбом оказался заунывным, банальным и монотонным, но и сам фильм получился ужасным. community_snippets.title: Letterboxd review of Brave
community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Brave"] Dunno how much of a novelty album films were in 1994, all I can say is 30+ years later this doesn't make much of an impression, unless you're already a huge fan of the music. Not unwatchable though.

community_snippets.title: Letterboxd review of Brave
community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Brave"] The lack of recognition of its astounding album 'Brave' by Marillion is undeniable. Unfortunately, this film doesn't portrait the idea of the album well. And it turns out to be a 'dark movie' and long music video that pretends to be shocking, but it lack of meaning. Neither the worst film nor a brilliant one. The idea could have been delivered better.

community_snippets.snippet: And so on. This is a great-looking movie, much enlivened by the inspiration of giving Merida three small brothers, little redheaded triplets. The Scottish Highlands are thrillingly painted in astonishing detail, and some action shows Merida's archery more than equal in assorted emergencies. "Brave" has an uplifting message about improving communication between mothers and daughters ...

community_snippets.title: Movie Review: Brave - California Literary Review
community_snippets.snippet: Brave is a good mainstream counterpart to another recent film, a visually inventive, but narratively lacking, Irish production called The Secret Of Kells. The enduring popularity of Celtic myths and music will always make this kind of story a safe bet for success, but some must inevitably turn out better than the rest.
